Emma —

Thanks for the questionnaire. Below are our written responses to the specific residency/retention items in the doc. I've kept answers concise; happy to expand on any item.

1) Can customer data leave the EU?
- Short answer: No by default for EU-region tenants.
- Details: For customers who select an EU region at provisioning, request payloads, generated outputs, and derived logs are stored and processed in EU-hosted clusters only. Data replication to other regions does not occur unless explicitly enabled via contractual addendum for business continuity or a specific cross-region feature. Backups for EU tenants are kept in encrypted storage in the EU; cross-region restore requires an approved support workflow and explicit customer approval.

2) Default retention windows (hosted API):
- Request/response payloads: default retention is 30 days for troubleshooting/quality purposes.
- Short-term operational traces (warm caches, transient logs): retained up to 7 days and then overwritten by circular buffers.
- Audit/security logs (auth events, policy evaluations): retained 90 days by default for incident investigation.
- Aggregate/metrics telemetry (non-PHI, aggregated): retained 365 days.

Notes: We offer customer-configurable retention tiers (30/90/365) via the Console for Enterprise plans; longer retention requires a data processing addendum. All retention periods are configurable at onboarding.

3) Customer-initiated erasure and data access requests
- Process: Customer submits erasure via the Console or an official support ticket (subject: Data Erasure Request). We perform automated deletion of customer-scoped request/response artifacts within 5 business days.
- Verification: We validate requestor identity via the account owner or preconfigured legal contact.
- Backups: Backups are immutable for short windows; logical deletion is performed on primary stores and any subsequent backup snapshots are rotated out per the backup TTL (see #5). We provide a deletion certificate showing timestamps and scopes after completion.

4) Deletion completeness & evidence
- We remove pointers and primary copies; forensic-level eradication from physical media is subject to standard cloud provider wipe/retention processes. For EU customers requiring stronger guarantees we offer add-on data disposition SLAs and can provide attestation language for contracts.

5) Backups and disaster recovery
- Backup frequency: daily snapshots for stateful metadata and weekly snapshots for other ancillary stores.
- Backup retention: default 30 days for EU tenants; extended retention available with an add-on.
- Encryption: all backups encrypted in transit and at rest using customer-shared KMS keys where configured.

6) Key management and encryption
- Data at rest: AES-256 encryption.
- KMS: Customers may bring their own key (BYOK) via customer-managed KMS (supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers can use our managed KMS or an enterprise BYOK integration). Keys and key rotation policies are documented in our security controls.

7) Cross-border subprocessors and subprocessors list
- We provide a current subprocessors list on request and include subprocessor notifications in our DPA. By default, no cross-border transfer for EU-region tenants except where expressly permitted.

8) Access controls and personnel
- Only authorized operations and SRE staff with role-based access can reach production clusters; access is logged and reviewed. We offer customer-facing audit logs for admin-level actions.

9) Retention of cached model context (KV cache)
- KV caches are ephemeral and exist only for the life of the session; default TTL is 24 hours and they are zeroed when sessions terminate. Caches are not persisted to long-term storage.

10) Contact for formal attestation / DPA language
- Rafael (cc'd) can provide contractual language and a DPA addendum for TerraPay's procurement/legal team. For SOC 2 and other artifacts, please see attached snapshot.

Attachment: redwood-soc2-snapshot-2028.pdf (pdf)
